description: Real-time quest language feedback: targets, quest words, grammar corrections and objective accuracy, pronunciation, milestones (src/language-learning/quest-feedback.ts).
comparison: exact, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent); an unknown op or step is an error, never a skip

cases.name: targets: words, patterns and phrases, de-duplicated; required counts
run: quest words, grammar corrections and objective accuracy, pronunciation, hints and milestones
cases.note: Objective 0 takes two of its targetWords (requiredCount 2): an incorrect use counts nothing, and a word outside targetWords counts nothing toward it, so beurre completes it and the words are done. Objectives 1 (practice_grammar) and 3 (grammar_drill) are grammar objectives to the lifecycle (normalizeObjectiveType: grammar; PL.core-grammar-objective-type, U120(4)): they take no word, and the one correct grammar feedback is one grammar use toward each (1 of 2, uses), the corrected one none. A runner that still reads them as use_vocabulary counts the words toward 10 for them, so its words are not done and it counts no grammar use. GrammarTriggerAnalyzer's objectives match a pattern exactly, then by containment.

cases.name: run: objectives with no target words take any word, each once, toward requiredCount (default 10); no grammar focus means no objectives
cases.note: practice_grammar is a grammar objective to the lifecycle (grammar, default 2; PL.core-grammar-objective-type, U120(4)), so it takes no word: the words required are 2 + 10, not 2 + 10 + 10 as when it was use_vocabulary, and the third word counts toward objective 1 only. The corrected feedback is no grammar use; the two correct ones complete it, with the halfway and complete milestones.

cases.name: run: the recent feedback keeps the last twenty items; a focus with an empty pattern list tracks 'general'
lifecycle: the second set is not read: vocabularyWords and required leave an objective taking any word toward 10
cases.note: The lifecycle reads targetWords and requiredCount only. Babylon's tracker read these fields as two listed words, two required; the strip now reads them as the lifecycle does: any word, default 10.

cases.name: lifecycle: a word outside the objective's targetWords does not advance the strip; a word counts once; an incorrect use counts nothing
cases.note: Unreal run 14 p9h-core shot 2: the strip counted words outside the quest, so it read Words 2/2 while the lifecycle's objective was open.

cases.name: lifecycle: the strip stays at the cap: a fifth quest word reads 2/2, never 5/2
cases.note: Five target words, two required: the second completes the objective and the third, fourth and fifth change nothing (the strip read Words 4/2 done before).

cases.name: lifecycle: the strip reads done only when the lifecycle completes every vocabulary objective, not when every listed word is used
cases.note: Objective 0 completes at two of its three words (the strip waited for all three before); objective 1 takes any word toward 3; the talk objective is not the strip's. Done, and its milestone, come with the word that completes the last vocabulary objective.

cases.name: lifecycle: every vocabulary type takes requiredCount, 10 when it is absent or 0; targetWords compare case-folded
lifecycle: a locked objective: the strip follows the lifecycle's records, so it never reads done while the lifecycle holds the objective open
cases.note: The strip knows no locks. The words objective has order 2 and the talk order 1, so the lifecycle counts no word until the talk; a host takes the lifecycle's records (QuestLifecycle.quests(), by index) with the lifecycle step. lifecycleSteps are the lifecycle steps the host ran before reading the records; the strip does not read them.

cases.name: lifecycle: a strip built from the lifecycle's records starts where the lifecycle is (a loaded quest), and takes a word the lifecycle counted that the strip never saw
cases.note: Objective 1 was restored complete with no count (an objective_complete fact): it reads 2 of 2. The host fed lait to the lifecycle only (a collection, say); the lifecycle step takes the lifecycle's records, so the strip completes with it, and sel afterwards changes nothing.

cases.name: pronunciation: the strip cannot read done before the lifecycle's pass count: two listed phrases passed once each are 2 of 4, not done
cases.note: The lifecycle counts passes of any phrase toward requiredCount (4) and matches no phrase to the objective. Babylon's tracker was done once every listed phrase had passed (after the second step). A fail below 60 is a retry (no attempt); a fail at 60 or more is an attempt that counts nothing; a pass after completion changes nothing (the cap).

cases.name: pronunciation: a locked pronunciation objective counts nothing; a completion the strip saw or the lifecycle's records unlock it
cases.note: Objective 2 (order 2) is locked until the talk (order 1) completes, and dependsOn the words objective p0. Passes made while it is locked count nothing, here and in the lifecycle. The words objective completes on the strip's own use; the talk completes in the lifecycle only, and the lifecycle step takes its record. Objective 3 dependsOn the pronunciation objective p2: merci counts nothing until p2 completes on the strip's own pass, then counts. lifecycleSteps are the lifecycle steps the host ran before reading the records; the strip does not read them.

cases.name: pronunciation: the locks are read once per attempt: a pass that completes a pronunciation objective unlocks its dependants for the next pass, not this one
cases.note: One attempt is one host event (trackHostEvent): the lifecycle takes the eligible objectives before the attempt (forEachObjective) and does not re-read a lock an objective of the same attempt released. The first pass completes a (listen_and_repeat, requiredCount 1, order 1); b (dependsOn a) and c (order 2) were locked when it began, so they count nothing on it. The second pass counts 1 for b and completes c; the third completes b. A strip that re-read each lock after a completion would count the first pass for b and c too.

cases.name: pronunciation: a strip built from the lifecycle's records starts where the lifecycle is (a loaded quest), and takes a pass the lifecycle counted that the strip never saw
cases.note: Objective 0 was saved at 1 of 4 passes; objective 1 was restored complete with no count (an objective_complete fact) and reads 1 of 1: the strip starts at 2 of 5. The host fed one pass to the lifecycle only; the lifecycle step takes the records, so the strip reads 3 of 5 and earns the halfway milestone, and the next two passes complete it as they complete the lifecycle's.

cases.name: pronunciation: an objective restored failed (maxAttempts) counts nothing more, so the strip is never done
cases.note: Objective 0 was saved failed at its two attempts (the lifecycle's failed flag): a pass at 90 completes objective 1 and does nothing for objective 0, here and in the lifecycle (open question 3: the quest stays active).

cases.name: pronunciation: every pronunciation type takes requiredCount, 3 when it is absent or 0; required is not read; the aliases are the lifecycle's
cases.note: pronounce is pronunciation_check and repeat is listen_and_repeat to the lifecycle (normalizeObjectiveType); speak_phrase keeps its name. Babylon's tracker read required (1, so done after one pass) and counted 1 for an objective listing no phrase.

cases.name: pronunciation: the lifecycle's own pass rules: a difficulty re-decides the pass, maxAttempts fails an objective for good, minAverageScore holds completion
cases.note: Objective 0 (beginner, pass at 40) passes on a host fail at 45. Objective 1 (advanced, pass at 70): 45 is a retry (below 60, no attempt), and 65 and 66, host passes, are failed attempts; the second reaches maxAttempts 2, so it has failed and the strip is never done. Objective 2 (minAverageScore 70) counts its passes but completes only when the mean of every score it took, the retry included, reaches 70: 45, 65, 66 and 100 average 69; the second 100 makes 75.2. Its count passes requiredCount meanwhile; the strip stays at the cap. The lifecycle step takes the records (a failed objective stays failed), and a later pass at 100 counts nothing for it.

cases.name: pronunciation: a fail below 60 is a retry that spends no attempt, and a fail at 60 spends one (the retry threshold, PL.core-p9-corpus-gaps)
cases.note: PRONUNCIATION_RETRY_THRESHOLD is 60: a fail scoring under 60 is a retry, a fail at 60 or more is a counted attempt. Objective 0 (maxAttempts 2): 59 is a retry, 60 its first attempt, 59 a retry, and the pass at 95 its second attempt, which completes it. Objective 1 (maxAttempts 1): the fail at 60 is its one attempt, so it has failed and the pass at 95 counts nothing; the strip is never done. With the threshold at 0 every fail is an attempt, so objective 0 fails at 60 as well; at 59 the first 59 is an attempt and objective 0 fails at 60; at 61 (or with 60 counted a retry) objective 1 never fails and completes at 95.

cases.name: grammar: practice_grammar and grammar_drill count grammar uses toward requiredCount (default 2), never words: ten correct words leave them at 0
cases.note: A runner that reads them as use_vocabulary (as the lifecycle did) completes both on the tenth word and reads the words done with three vocabulary objectives; here the words are one objective of 1, and the grammar objectives wait for grammar uses. A corrected feedback and one in no target language count nothing; each correct one counts one toward each open grammar objective: objective 0 completes at 2, objective 1 at 3 (the halfway milestone when the count crosses half, 4 of 5; complete when the last completes), and a use after that counts nothing more.

cases.name: grammar: the aliases, the default and the locks: a grammar objective locked when the feedback arrives counts nothing, and one feedback never completes a grammar objective and the one it unlocks
cases.note: grammar_pattern and grammar_activities (the hydrator's names for practice_grammar/2 and grammar_activities/1), conjugation and grammar are all grammar to the lifecycle. requiredCount 0 or absent is 2. The first feedback completes gp (order 1); grammar_activities (order 2) and conjugation (dependsOn gp) were locked when it arrived, so they count it not; the bare grammar objective counts it.

cases.name: grammar: a load from the lifecycle's records starts at the saved count, and a sync takes the lifecycle's count when the host fed it a use the strip did not see
cases.note: Objective 0 was saved at 1 of 3, objective 1 complete at 2, and objective 2 (conjugate) complete with no count saved: a completed objective counts its required number in full (2), so the strip starts at 5 of 7. The correct feedback puts objective 0 at 2; the host then fed the lifecycle one more use (lifecycleSteps), and the lifecycle step takes its records: objective 0 complete at 3, and the strip is done with the complete milestone.
